name: Geometric sans
summary: A sans serif built from the circle, the square and the triangle: a round o, a single-storey a, pointed apexes and almost no contrast. It is the type of the modernist programme, clean and optimistic, with a small x-height in the classic cuts.

philosophy.core_thesis: A letter is a construction of pure forms, free of the hand and of history.
design_principles: Draw the o, c, e and the bowls of b, d, p and q from a near-perfect circle.
Keep the stroke contrast at 1.0–1.3:1, measured on the o.
Use a single-storey a and g, and pointed apexes on A, M, N, V and W.
Hold the x-height at 0.58–0.70 of the cap height in the classic cuts, so the ascenders are long.
Give the capitals the widths of their figures: a circular O, a square-wide M, a narrow E and S.
Set headlines with tight tracking (−0.02 to −0.04 em) and short lines.
anti_patterns: Calligraphic stress or angled pen terminals

classification.note: Many modern faces mix geometric capitals with a humanist or neo-grotesque lower case; the test is the round o and the single-storey a.

anatomy.contrast: None or almost none: the thin parts are 0.8–1.0 of the stem.
anatomy.stress: None: the strokes keep one weight round the o.
anatomy.serifs: None: the strokes end clean, with no serif.
anatomy.terminals: Cut straight, at a right angle to the stroke.
anatomy.aperture: Moderate: the c is a circle with a wedge removed.
anatomy.key_letters: A circular o, a single-storey a, pointed apexes on A, M and N, and a t without a hook in the classic cuts.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.58–0.70 of the cap height in the classic cuts; screen faces such as Poppins go higher.
metrics.contrast: The side of the o is 1.0 to 1.3 times as thick as its top.
metrics.width: Round letters are wide and others narrow; the mean advance of a to z is 0.42–0.52 em.

setting.text_sizes: Set text at 10–12 pt in print and 16–19 px on screen; the small x-height needs the larger sizes.
setting.display_sizes: Set titles at 32–200 px, often in bold or in capitals.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 1.4–1.6 for text and 1.0–1.1 for titles.
setting.tracking: Set 0 to +0.01 em in text, −0.02 to −0.04 em in large titles, +0.1 em for capital labels.
setting.measure: Set 45–65 characters a line; the round letters make lines feel long.
setting.case_and_features: Use capitals for short labels and logos; use the alternates of the family for a circular a only if all a forms agree.

pairing.rule: Pair it with a serif of strong contrast for titles or a quiet serif for long text; avoid a second sans.

pairs.why: Both are constructed faces; the contrast of the Didone sets off the even sans.
The Garalde carries text better at small sizes, and the geometric sans carries headings and labels.

reference_faces.note: Jost takes its forms from the German geometric sans of the 1920s. The default instance of League Spartan in google/fonts is Thin, so the specimen uses Jost.

emotion.target_response: Optimism and order: the reader feels a clean, forward-looking modern voice.

avoid_when: Long text must read well at small sizes on a screen.
The brief asks for warmth from the hand or a bookish voice.

modifiers.how: Open the forms to classical widths, use a two-storey a, and raise the x-height to 0.70.
Make the o oval, even the widths and raise the x-height to 0.74.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
